PUBLIC RESPONSE: 4 and 11

The piece is a dialogue sestina on the six end-words mountains, valleys, forests, music, morning, evening. The retrograde 6-1-5-2-4-3 rotation is intact through Stanzas 1-12 and the envoi 73-75 pairs mountains/valleys, forests/music and morning/evening correctly, so the formal defect is not a broken end-word sequence but a displaced couplet inside the opening invocation.

Strephon 1-6 and Klaius 7-12 are set up as parallel appeals. The fourth and third positions of the two opening stanzas are the invocations:

4 Vouchsafe your silent ears to plaining music,
11 Vouchsafe you silent ears to plaining music,

Both lines are the music position of their respective stanzas, 4 is the 4th place of Stanza 1 and 11 is the 5th place of Stanza 2 in the 6-1-5-2-4-3 rotation, and both end-word music is preserved, so the sestina surface is unchanged. The wording is otherwise essentially identical with only the pronoun your / you shifted, and the same Vouchsafe... plaining music formula is duplicated across the speaker change. In the original disposition the Strephon appeal should stay with Strephon and the Klaius reply with Klaius. The two nearly verbatim invocation lines have been transposed between the two opening stanzas, breaking the speaker-parallelism while leaving the end-word pattern formally intact. Restoring 4 and 11 to their proper speakers restores the intended mirrored invocation.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: 28 and 74

The six-image cycle that governs each six-line Strephon/Klaius block is broken in the Strephon block that opens at line 25. In a regular block the six pastoral tokens mountains, valleys, forests, music, morning and evening each occur once. 

Lines 25-30 as printed give:
25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music; — forests / music
26 Hath made itself a crier of the morning, — morning
27 And hath with wailing strength climbed highest mountains; — mountains
28 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests; — forests
29 Long since I see my joys come to their evening, — evening
30 And state thrown down to over-trodden valleys. — valleys

Forests is duplicated in 25 and 28 and the block is missing a clean music subject for the 26-27 “Hath made … And hath …” couplet. The couplet needs a singular subject that can “make itself a crier” and that carries the music token.

The line that is sitting at the very close of the dialogue, 74,

Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music

is a Long since line with an explicit music subject, exactly the kind of subject the 26-27 couplet wants, and it is the only Long since line in the poem that carries music. It belongs in the middle of the Strephon block where the Long since pair 28-29 is formed, and it would restore the six-image set to forests / morning / mountains / forests / evening / valleys once line 28 is moved out.

Line 28,

Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests;

is a classic closing Long since summing-up that fits much better as the penultimate spoken line before the final communal couplet. With 28 moved to the end it pairs naturally with

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.

giving the expected terminal triad mountains/valleys; forests/music; morning/evening, while line 74 takes its place in the Strephon 25-30 block and supplies the missing music subject for the “Hath made itself a crier…” lines. That is the swap that restores the strict form.

74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music            D
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.        E F

So C forests is absent from the tornada and the line that has to leave the envoi is 74. That much is settled.

Where I part from a straight 25↔74 swap is the Strephon block 25-30. The printed block is

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;
26 Hath made itself a crier of the morning,
27 And hath with wailing strength climbed highest mountains;
28 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests;
29 Long since I see my joys come to their evening,
30 And state thrown down to over-trodden valleys.

25 is the grammatical head for the Hath-made couplet 26-27. These forests eke… Hath made itself… And hath with wailing strength… is a single syntactic unit. Pull 25 out and 26-27 are left subjectless in the printed text, a visible textual defect independent of end-word bookkeeping.

The block also shows a concrete duplication that the sestina rotation is meant to avoid: forests occurs internally in 25 and again as the ending word of 28 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests. The block is also missing a clean Long since music subject to pair with the Long since pair 28-29 that the stanza is building.

74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music is the only Long since line in the poem that ends with music and is the natural Long since music subject the middle of the block wants. Conversely 28 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests is a summative Long since line of the sort that belongs at the close of the dialogue, immediately before the communal couplet.

Put 28 into the tornada in place of 74 and keep 25-27 intact. The envoi then reads

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;
74 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests;
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.

with the forests image now present in the closing triad and the terminal triad restored to mountains/valleys — forests — morning/evening. The body stanza retains its These forests eke… Hath made… And hath… unit, the duplicate forests token in 25-28 is removed, and a Long since music subject is supplied where the Long since music pattern belongs.

The swap that does that is the present line 28 with the present line 74.

I’m fully with the sestina diagnosis you’ve laid out, and I agree the envoi is the problem. The six tokens mountains / valleys / forests / music / morning / evening rotate correctly through 1-72 and the two blocks repeat the 1 2 3 4 5 6 / 6 1 5 2 4 3 … permutation. As printed

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;   A B
74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music              D
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.          E F

we have A B, D, E F and no forests in the closing triad. 74 has to leave the tornada, that much is settled.

Where I think the 25/74 swap goes wrong is in the body. The Strephon stanza 25-30 is printed as

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;
26 Hath made itself a crier of the morning,
27 And hath with wailing strength climbed highest mountains;
28 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests;
29 Long since I see my joys come to their evening,
30 And state thrown down to over-trodden valleys.

25-27 is one syntactic unit. 25 supplies the subject These forests eke… and 26-27 are the dependent Hath-made / And-hath continuation. Pull 25 out and 26-27 are left subjectless. That is a much more visible break than an end-word bookkeeping issue, and it removes the only internal C … D collocation that is doing real thematic work in that stanza.

There is also a very obvious textual flaw in the printed stanza: forests is duplicated. 25 contains forests internally and 28 ends with forests. A sestina stanza should use each image once. The stanza is also missing the Long since music subject it is clearly building toward: 28-29 are a Long since pair, and the whole middle of the poem is built on Long since summations. 74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music is the only Long since line in the poem that ends with music and it is the natural Long since music subject for that block.

The elegant fix is to keep the 25-27 forests eke… Hath made… And hath… unit intact, put the Long since music subject where the Long since pair belongs, and move a forests-closing summation to the envoi where the dialogue needs a closing forest image before the communal couplet. Put 74 into the body in place of 28 and put 28 into the tornada in place of 74.

The body then reads

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;   D
26 Hath made itself a crier of the morning,          E
27 And hath with wailing strength climbed highest mountains; A
28 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music        C? 
29 Long since I see my joys come to their evening,   F
30 And state thrown down to over-trodden valleys.    B

with the forests + music collocation retained at 25, the duplicate forests removed, and a clean Long since music line sitting next to the Long since evening line. The subject of 26-27 is preserved.

The tornada becomes

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;
74 Long since my thoughts more desert be than forests;
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.

73 is A B, 74 now supplies the forest closing summation before the communal couplet, and 75 is E F. The forests token is restored to the closing triad, the Long since summative line is where a penultimate spoken line belongs, and the body keeps its syntactic integrity.

That is the transposition of the present lines 28 and 74. The 25/74 swap solves the tornada on paper but at the cost of breaking the 25-27 syntactic unit and leaving two music-ending lines to trade places with no real gain.
